issues.description: The problem statement UML and the solution implementation expect a Stock method named addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient), but the template Stock class provides a method named addItem(StockIngredient) instead. This name/signature mismatch will cause students' SealSaloon implementation (which should call addToStockIngredients when accepting deliveries) to fail to compile against the provided template.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the specification and solution by renaming the template method addItem(StockIngredient) to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient), or add a wrapper method addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) that delegates to addItem. This ensures students can implement SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery as described without compilation errors.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML) and the solution expect a Stock method named addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient), but the template Stock implementation provides addItem(StockIngredient) instead. This mismatch means students reading the specification or following the solution will look for addToStockIngredients while the starter code exposes addItem, creating an unnecessary mapping burden when they implement or call the Stock API.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method addItem(StockIngredient) to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) to match the UML in the problem statement and the solution, or add a delegating method addToStockIngredients that calls addItem to preserve compatibility.
